subject: Social Media
title: Echo Chambers Explained
description: A 60-second lesson on Echo Chambers Explained.

hook.text: You post an opinion. Everyone agrees. You feel validated. But you're only hearing your own side.

buildup.text: Echo chambers aren't new. Humans always chose like-minded groups. Algorithms just accelerate it.

discovery.text: Cass Sunstein warned in 2001: internet groups amplify extreme views through repeated agreement.

twist.text: Research shows echo chambers are rarer than feared. Most people see diverse views—and just ignore them.

climax.text: The real danger isn't isolation. It's seeing opponents without understanding their reasoning.

punchline.text: Hearing the other side isn't enough.

quiz.question: According to research, what's the real danger of echo chambers?
